What If Stellantis Allowed SRT To Bring Back the GTX Nameplate Based on a 1970s Plymouth – Rendering
9 photos
Photo: adry53customs / Instagram
Stellantis is currently preparing for the upcoming 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, and they have already revealed what’s new from Dodge – an exclusive Mopar '27 bundle available for the 2027 Charger R/T and Scat Pack Plus models to celebrate 90 years of Mopar, though only on 270 examples.
The 2026 SEMA Show is just around the corner, and, unsurprisingly, Stellantis joins the event to showcase what’s new from its variety of brands. Dodge took off with the Charger R/T and Scat Pack Plus fastback coupe variants wearing the Mopar '27 package, but we bet there will be more on offer.
Actually, the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI are also ready to contribute. For example, Timothy Adry Emmanuel, the virtual artist better known as " adry53customs " on social media, continues his dream ride periplus within the CGI car world with a focus on Stellantis lately.
Not long ago, he created the virtual Dodge Copperhead Concept to potentially bring back the Challenger in an unofficial, hypothetical design project as a longtail model specifically created to fight the likes of the Ford Mustang GTD. It was envisioned as an “update for the Challenger model but with a longtail treatment on the back,” inspired by Stellantis’ roster at the Paris Motor Show but rocking America’s muscle car style with a 1,000+ horsepower V8 powertrain and a sport chassis that would allow it to compete with the mighty GTD.
Now, he switches his attention to the defunct label Plymouth, because “after doing the longtail Challenger concept I decided to bring more American Muscle cars with longer tail and I think one of the best candidates for a modern reinterpretation is the GTX, or the Satellite, or the Roadrunner from 1971-1972.”
He imagines that his design project could be made by Dodge as the revival of the SRT GTX nameplate and in place of the Super Bee, instead rocking a Hemi V8 and Plum Crazy attire. Basically, his idea is modelled after the Plymouth GTX from 1971, an upscale mid-size muscle car based on the B-body architecture as a two-door hardtop featuring the mighty 426 and 440ci V8s of the company.
The modern reinterpretation features the same double round front lights, now in LED, the pointy front end, and even the cowl induction hood with black plastics on top of it, as well as the rectangular rear lights, now also LEDs. But the contemporary creation now has a widebody style complete with a similar profile, again blending the retro-modern cues that have become so famous as of late across the automotive industry. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Timothy Adry Emmanuel (@adry53customs)
